Units are worth their point cost in VP when destroyed by end of round 5. Units at or below half strength are worth 50% of their cost. Single-model units use remaining Wounds/HP to determine value.

Hold an objective by keeping at least one model within 3" of it with no enemy model in range. If an enemy model is in range, the objective is contested and scores for nobody. Each unit can only hold or contest ONE objective per turn — if it qualifies for several, roll to decide which. Elevation: a unit can capture or contest an objective directly one level above or below it. Control is lost the moment no friendly model is within the 3" radius, or an enemy model enters it.
After round 5, count all VP for each side. A player wins by having at least 100 more VP than the opponent. Otherwise the game is a draw.
Used by all missions unless stated otherwise. Each secondary objective is worth 200 VP.

For objective-marker missions only. When an objective outside any deployment zone is controlled for the first time, roll a die — on 5+ it becomes a relic worth +100 extra VP at game end.
Your highest-cost HQ unit must survive to end of round 5. If tied, choose before deployment.
The enemy's highest-cost HQ unit must be destroyed by end of round 5. If tied, opponent chooses before deployment.
Objective Deployment
Divide the board into four quarters and place an objective marker in the middle of each.
Both players roll a die; the highest score picks which quarter to deploy in. The other player's deployment zone is the opposite quarter.
Starting with the winner of the roll, both players alternate deploying one unit at a time.
No unit can be deployed within 9" of the centre of the table at game start.

To control a table quarter, a unit must control the mission objectives inside it. A unit can only occupy one quarter — if spread over more than one, roll randomly. At the end of each battle round, a player scores 200 VP per controlled table quarter.
Wreckage (×9) Deployment
Place 9 mission objectives (wreckage) evenly distributed on the field.
Both players roll a die; the winner chooses which table edge to deploy along. Their opponent gets the opposite edge.

To collect wreckage, a unit must be in direct base contact with the objective and use a Stand & Shoot command to pick it up — and it may do nothing else but fight back in melee for that activation. Only units able to control a mission objective can pick up wreckage. Securing wreckage scores 200 VP per piece; the objective is then removed. Additionally, VP are awarded for destroyed enemy units.
Objective Command Post
Place one command post in each deployment zone (Position: 12" in, 12" up from corner).
Place three objectives in a line between both deployment zones.

Each command post has an enhanced scanner and jammer: no model may be deployed within 18" of the enemy command post by any means. Enemy units that scatter into this zone from Deep Strike are sent back to reserves.
Both players roll a die; the winner chooses deployment side. Alternate deploying one unit at a time.

Controlling one objective at end of a battle round scores 200 VP. If a player occupies the enemy's command post, they win automatically regardless of VP. If both lose their command posts in the same round, the higher VP player wins.
Place one objective in the middle of the table.
Place two objectives in diagonally opposing quarters (12" in, 12" up from corner).
Place the remaining two objectives in the two empty quarters (24" in, 12" up).
Both players roll a die; highest score chooses deployment zone. Alternate deploying one unit at a time.
No unit may deploy within 9" of the table centre at game start.
Controlling one objective at end of a battle round scores 200 VP (up to 600 VP per round). The player with the most VP at game end wins.
Relic Deployment

A creature unit must end a battle round in direct base contact with the relic to control it. The relic moves with the unit (max 6"/round); if any rule would move the unit further, the relic is left behind. The relic can never embark on a transport and is left behind if the controlling unit does so. If the controlling unit is in melee or both sides are in base contact, it is contested. Scoring starts in the second battle round — from then on, controlling the relic at the end of a Battle round scores 400 VP, or 800 VP if within own deployment zone. Additionally, VP are awarded for destroyed enemy units.
Center (400 VP) Flanks (200 VP)
Place two objectives on the same horizontal line at opposing ends, 6" from each board edge.
At end of each battle round: controlling a side objective scores 200 VP; controlling the middle objective scores 400 VP. The player with the most VP at game end wins.
